assumptions: Labels are stipulated fictional belief contents, not measured LLM or human beliefs.
The token occupies exactly one of two places at the end of each scene.
People remember their last observation and update it after an observed move or a trusted current-location message; they do not infer unobserved moves.
Both people see the initial placement together; the sender observes the later move.
An absent reader does not learn that a move occurred and receives no other update.
The sender cannot observe actual reader attendance and treats the particular attendance display as accurate; no other attendance information is available.
The display can disagree with actual attendance in the authored narrator's record, but its possible unreliability is not information available to the sender.
Every authored world changes location, but this is an authoring invariant, not a public rule known to the reader.
Prior scenes contain no sent or planned message and no unspecified future-message target.
Delivered-current controls contain a truthful current-location message, trusted receipt by the reader, and confirmation observed by the sender.
The fixed claim is that the token is in place_b; 1 means that claim is true under the queried perspective, not that a belief is accurate.
Messages stop before perspective questions and before any generated answer; labels and IDs are metadata, never part of those messages.
Four wording templates train, two validate, and two test; this is wording/template holdout, not held-out story-family generalization.
Delivered-current rows have split control and must not be used for fitting.
Materials require independent human review before any human-validity claim.
